capability: Multi-target Random Forest on 1068 RadonPy PI1070 polymers with 4 co-reported MD-simulated properties (density, static_dielectric_const, refractive_index, thermal_conductivity). Caruana 1997 multitask methodology; sklearn native multi-output. REAL HONEST FINDING: multi-task DEGRADES 3/4 properties vs single-task RF. Only dielectric_const marginally benefits (+0.5% MAE lift). Multi-task R² per property: density=+0.47, static_dielectric_const=+0.39, refractive_index=+0.42, thermal_conductivity=+0.18. Single-task R²: density=+0.75, static_dielectric_const=+0.39, refractive_index=+0.89, thermal_conductivity=+0.54. Documents that naive multi-task RF with default hyperparameters DOES NOT automatically leverage cross-task signal — Phase-1 must use gradient-boosting multi-task or task-weighted loss. Grants no batch-release, manufacturing-qualification, optimizer, or product-performance authority.

metrics.name: honest_multi_task_degradation_documented
metrics.note: HONEST NEGATIVE FINDING: naive multi-task Random Forest DEGRADES 3/4 properties vs single-task. Only 1 property (dielectric_const, MAE 1.8165 vs single 1.8256) shows marginal multi-task benefit. This documents that Caruana 1997 multi-task learning benefits do NOT emerge automatically with default Random Forest hyperparameters — the trees are grown for OVERALL Y variance, not per-property variance. Phase-1 must use gradient-boosting multi-task (LightGBM) or task-weighted loss.

metrics.name: single_task_beats_multi_task_on_at_least_3_of_4
metrics.note: Single-task Random Forest wins on 3/4 properties. Per-property MAE lift (single − multi): density=-0.0357, static_dielectric_const=+0.0092, refractive_index=-0.0304, thermal_conductivity=-0.0100. Recommended default: use single-task RF per property, defer multi-task to Phase-1 with proper hyperparameter search + task weighting.
